captions.instagram:
How does concept art work?

Before a film builds a single set, someone paints it. Design a robot auto-rickshaw from twelve black silhouettes, paint a monsoon street in greys then colour, paint over a 3D blockout, and draw a forest spirit from every side.

→ Before a film builds anything, concept artists design it on paper.
→ Artists start with dozens of tiny black silhouettes, each made in a minute or two.
→ Pick the shape that reads best, and it grows into a drawing, then a 3D model.
→ Painters solve light and dark in greys first, then brush colour over the top.
→ Haze makes far things paler and bluer: atmospheric perspective fakes depth.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/conceptartclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does concept art work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Before a film builds a single set, someone paints it. Design a robot auto-rickshaw from twelve black silhouettes, paint a monsoon street in greys then colour, paint over a 3D blockout, and draw a forest spirit from every side.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/conceptartclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/conceptartclear

In this video:
• A design document for the whole crew. Concept art decides what a film's world, characters and objects look like before anyone builds them.
• Dozens of tiny black shapes. Artists start with thumbnails: quick, stamp-sized sketches, often solid black silhouettes.
• Value first, then colour. Painters plan the lights and darks in greys before choosing colours.
• Block out in 3D, then paint over. Environment artists often build a quick grey 3D blockout of a set, pick a camera and paint over the render.
• Every side, at the same scale. Once a design is chosen, a turnaround shows it from the front, side and back without perspective, so everything can be measured.
• New tools, same thinking. Pencil and gouache gave way to Photoshop (1990), layers (1994), pen tablets, Procreate (2011), 3D paint-overs and photobashing.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
